<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />Stade, as the equivalent of ''ō'' ({{GHGheb|text=קֹֽבָה־לִּי}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGpar|9|v}}). Still more surprising is {{GHGheb|text=קָבְנוֹ|translate=curse him}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, for {{GHGheb|text=קֻבֶּ֫נּוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=קָבּ׳}}.<ref>For {{GHGheb|text=נוֹ}} as suffix of the 3rd person a parallel might be found in {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁנוֹ}}, {{GHGpar|100|o}}, and probably also in the ''Nûn'' of the Phoenician suffix {{GHGheb|text=נם}}: cf. Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xli. p. 643, and the note on {{GHGpar|100|o}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|p}}
3. Examples with ''Pathaḥ'' in the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} are {{GHGheb|text=בַּר}} (in {{GHGheb|text=לְבָרָם|translate=to prove them}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=18}}); {{GHGheb|text=רָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שַׁךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּשַׁגָּם|translate=in their error}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=3}} (so ed. Mant., but there is also good authority for {{GHGheb|text=בְּשַׁגַּם}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ·}} = {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ·}} = {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} and {{GHGheb|text=גַּם}} also; so Baer and Ginsburg). Also {{GHGheb|text=גַּל|translate=take away}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=22}}; and the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַם|translate=it is hot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=6}}, &c. (on the ''ē'' of the preformative cf. n); {{GHGheb|text=יֵמַר|translate=it is bitter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵצַר|translate=it is straitened}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵרַךְ|translate=it is soft}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשַׁם|translate=it is desolate}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=19}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּשָֽׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=19}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּקַ֫ל|translate=she was despised}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=4}} (but elsewhere in the ''impf. consec.'' with the tone on the penultima, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫צֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=8}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫רַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=11}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=19|verse=7}}); in the 1st ''sing. imperfect'' {{GHGheb|text=אֵיתָ֑ם}}<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=6}}, instead of {{GHGheb|text=תִּישָׁ֑מְנָה}}, which could only come from {{GHGheb|text=ישׁם}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּי֚שׁ׳}} is intended, and {{GHGheb|text=יֶאְשְׁמוּ}} in the same verse is probably only an error for {{GHGheb|text=יֵשַׁ֫מּוּ}}.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=14}}, abnormally written fully for {{GHGheb|text=אֵתָם}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=אֶתָּם}} is to be read, as in some MSS., on the analogy of the 3rd sing. {{GHGheb|text=יִתֹּם}}.—In the ''impf. Qal'' of {{GHGheb|text=שׁלל}} the reading of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=8}} varies between {{GHGheb|text=יְשַׁלּ֫וּךָ}} (Baer, Ginsb.) and {{GHGheb|text=יְשָׁלּ֫וּךָ}} (ed. Mant., {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|Jabl.|Biblia Hebraica ex recensione D. E. Jablonski, Berolini, 1699.}}}}).— The following forms are to be explained with Barth ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xliii, p. 178) as imperfects Qal with original ''ĭ'' in the second syllable, there being no instances of their Hiphʿîl in the same sense: {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫גֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=5}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּסֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=40|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=4}}, &c.; perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=תְּצִלֶּ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=11}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָהֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Job|chapter=31|verse=26}}, &c.; in accordance with this last form, {{GHGheb|text=(בְּ)הִלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Job|chapter=29|verse=3}} would also be an {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}}, not Hiphʿîl (for {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֲהִלּוֹ}}), as formerly explained below, under w. Finally the very peculiar form {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫רִץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=53}} may probably be added to the list.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|q}}
Imperfects, with an original ''u'' in the second syllable, are also found with this ''ŭ'' lengthened to ''û'' (instead of ''ō''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָרוּן}}, if the text is correct, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=29|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=91|verse=6}} (unless it be simply an imperfect from {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּד|translate=to be powerful, to prevail}}); {{GHGheb|text=יָרוּץ}} (if from {{GHGheb|text=רצץ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=4}}, &c. (also defectively {{GHGheb|text=אָרֻץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=30}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=6}}, according to Baer, {{GHGheb|text=וְתָרוּץ}}); {{GHGheb|text=תִּתֻּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=11}} (on the sharpening of the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} cf. g above).<ref>According to Stade, {{GHGcite|title=Grammatik}}, § 95, Rem., the pronunciation with ''û'', since it also appears in Neo-Punic [and in Western Syriac, see Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title=Syr. Gramm.}}, § 48], was that of everyday life.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|r}}
A similar analogy with verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is soon in the infinitives {{GHGheb|text=לָבוּר}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בֹּר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּחֻקוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=27}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=בְּחוּקוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=29}}) for {{GHGheb|text=בְּחֻקּוֹ}}, and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲמֻֽשְׁךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=21}}. (The forms {{GHGheb|text=חַנּוֹת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁמּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַלּ֫וֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=11}}, formerly treated here as infinitives from {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} stems, are rather to be referred to {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems, with Barth, ''Wurzeluntersuchungen'', Lpz. 1902, p. 21.) On other similar cases, see below, under ee. For examples of the ''aramaïzing imperfect'', see above, g.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|s}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|participle}}, the aramaïzing form {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁאֲסַ֫יִךְ}} for {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁסְסַ֫יִךְ}} occurs in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=16}} (the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} indicates a {{GHGterm|participle}} from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁסָה}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֹעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=19}} appears to be a contraction from {{GHGheb|text=רֹֽעֲעָה}}, ''part. fem.'' = ''breaking in pieces.''<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
